reasoning: The two sets share most of their text: the same brief, nearly the same spec, architecture, pipelines, tests and 30-task M1 plan. A wins because it fixed several real defects that B still carries. B's contract makes `runlog.RunRecord.config: RunConfig` and `runlog.Checkpoint.methods: Mapping[str, MethodConfig]`, so runlog has to import train and methods. Its own architecture says `runlog` depends only on `core`, and `methods → runlog` makes that an import cycle. A turns both into plain data and states it ('so `runlog` imports neither `train` nor `methods`'). B keeps stale '3-checkpoint snake run' fixture cases after the change to 11 checkpoints. It also keeps a pipelines 'Open questions' section already settled by AD-10, and a TC-17 bound ('at most 1 of the 20 seeds') that will fail by chance about a quarter of the time; A corrects that to ≤4 with the binomial reasoning. B's spec widens Holm correction to 'all baseline comparisons in that world' while still requiring 'both nulls', and loosens the budget to 90 min and $10, against the brief's 'about an hour' and 'a few dollars'. A's task packets are more complete. M1-T09 includes Checkpoint, Transition, Step and Episode. M1-T17 includes Comparison, Checkpoint and WorldSpec. M1-T16 and M1-T17 create stub files for their thicken siblings, which B leaves undefined. The snake observation layout is pinned in `worlds.make`. A's exit criteria are precise ('TC-03 (check-discrete half)'), where B writes 'TC-10–TC-22 (snake parts)', a range that takes in fish and prey cases. A's main weakness is the roadmap: it splits the fish stage into M3/M5/M6 but numbers predator-prey M4 and lists it after M6, so the build order reads confusingly against the IDs. B's single M3 fish milestone is lopsided but simpler. Both share the same thin wiring tasks, the long block of 'order'-only dependency rows, and 'Sample: … (not written yet)' in their packets.

strengths: runlog decoupled from train/methods via plain-data config, matching the architecture's import directions
Precise M1 Exit and Deferred lists, including REPLAY, CHECK, NOTES and TRAIN-07 marked 'partly'
Packets include every type a spine needs (Checkpoint, Transition, Step, Comparison)
Statistically sound TC-17 bound; snake observation layout pinned in the contract
Stub files for thicken tasks created by the spine task, so the call path exists from the start
weaknesses: Milestone IDs out of order (M5, M6 before M4) make the build order confusing
CONSTRAINTS boundary line omits the charts → baselines edge that the architecture adds
Long block of 'order' dependency rows that add little
'CI nightly' mentioned in a solo project with no CI

strengths: Clear 4-milestone roadmap with IDs in build order
Same solid architecture, pipelines and golden cases as A on the shared parts
One fish milestone is simpler to follow
weaknesses: Contract creates a runlog↔train/methods dependency that contradicts the architecture
Stale '3-checkpoint' fixtures and an already-resolved Open questions section
Spec Holm-scope wording is inconsistent, and budget/GPU limits are loosened against the brief
M3 fish milestone is lopsided against the others
Architecture mentions CI that doesn't exist

M1-T17: packet lacks evaluate.Comparison, runlog.Checkpoint and core.WorldSpec, and the stats.py/verdict.py stubs it must call are in no task's Writes
